questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a painless genital ulcer with a clean base and indurated edges. Darkfield microscopy shows spirochetes. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (chancre) is treated with Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM as a single dose. This remains the gold standard first-line treatment.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on her trunk. Skin slit smear shows a Bacterial Index (BI) of 0. Nerve involvement shows only one nerve thickening. What is the WHO classification and treatment regimen?
opts: Multibacillary leprosy — 12 months MDT (Rifampicin + Clofazimine + Dapsone)
Paucibacillary leprosy — Dapsone monotherapy for 2 years
questions.exp: BI = 0 and 1–5 skin lesions classifies as Paucibacillary (PB) leprosy. WHO MDT for PB is Rifampicin 600 mg monthly + Dapsone 100 mg daily for 6 months.

questions.q: A 45-year-old patient with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis develops tense blisters on normal and erythematous skin. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Tense blisters with linear IgG and C3 deposition at the BMZ on DIF is classic for Bullous pemphigoid. Pemphigus shows intercellular IgG (fish-net pattern). Linear IgA shows linear IgA deposits.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with intensely pruritic vesicles symmetrically distributed on elbows, knees, and buttocks. Small bowel biopsy shows villous atrophy. DIF shows granular IgA at the dermal papillae. What is the treatment of choice?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhring's disease) presents with granular IgA at dermal papillae and is associated with gluten-sensitive enteropathy. Dapsone provides rapid relief; gluten-free diet is the long-term treatment.

questions.q: A 60-year-old farmer presents with a verrucous plaque on the foot present for 20 years. Histopathology shows 'copper penny bodies' (sclerotic cells). What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is characterized by 'copper penny bodies' (Medlar bodies/sclerotic cells) on histopathology. The most common causative organism is Fonsecaea pedrosoi.

questions.q: A 50-year-old immunosuppressed patient presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base following the T4 dermatome unilaterally. He complains of severe burning pain preceding the rash by 3 days. What is the most appropriate antiviral treatment?
opts: Acyclovir 800 mg 5 times daily for 7 days
Acyclovir 200 mg 5 times daily for 5 days
questions.exp: Herpes zoster in an immunocompromised patient requires high-dose Acyclovir 800 mg 5 times/day for 7 days (or IV acyclovir in severe cases). The standard herpes simplex dose (200 mg) is inadequate for VZV.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with malar rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and joint pain. ANA is positive with anti-dsDNA antibodies. She has proteinuria. Which skin finding is considered most specific for this condition?
opts: Discoid plaques with follicular plugging and scarring
questions.exp: While the butterfly rash is characteristic of SLE, discoid plaques with follicular plugging and scarring are the most specific cutaneous finding for lupus erythematosus. Gottron's papules are specific for dermatomyositis.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with well-demarcated silvery scaly plaques on the extensor surfaces and scalp. Histopathology shows parakeratosis, elongated rete ridges, neutrophilic infiltrate in the stratum corneum, and absence of granular layer. What are these neutrophilic collections called?
questions.exp: Munro microabscesses are neutrophilic collections in the parakeratotic stratum corneum, characteristic of psoriasis. Pautrier's microabscesses are seen in mycosis fungoides (epidermotropic T-cell lymphoma).

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with multiple painful genital ulcers with soft edges, necrotic base, and tender inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo). Culture on chocolate agar shows Gram-negative coccobacilli arranged in 'school of fish' pattern. What is the treatment?
questions.exp: Chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi) is treated with Azithromycin 1 g single oral dose, Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose, or Ciprofloxacin 500 mg BD for 3 days. Penicillin is used for syphilis.

questions.q: A neonate develops widespread erythema and superficial blistering within 48 hours of birth. The skin sheds on gentle pressure (Nikolsky sign positive). Blood cultures grow Staphylococcus aureus. What is the pathophysiology of this condition?
opts: Exfoliative toxins A and B cleave desmoglein-1 in the granular layer
Complement-mediated destruction of the basement membrane zone
questions.exp: Staphylococcal Scalded Skin Syndrome (SSSS) is caused by exfoliative toxins A and B from S. aureus, which cleave desmoglein-1 specifically in the granular layer, causing superficial blister formation at this level.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with sclerodactyly, Raynaud's phenomenon, telangiectasias on face, and dysphagia. ANA shows anti-centromere antibody pattern. Which complication is she LEAST likely to develop compared to diffuse systemic sclerosis?
questions.exp: This is CREST syndrome (limited cutaneous SSc). Anti-centromere antibodies are associated with limited SSc. Scleroderma renal crisis (SRC) with malignant hypertension is predominantly seen in diffuse SSc with anti-topoisomerase (anti-Scl-70) antibodies.

questions.q: A 70-year-old woman presents with a pearly translucent nodule with rolled edges and telangiectasias on the nose, slowly growing over 2 years, with central ulceration. What is the Mohs micrographic surgery cure rate for this lesion?
questions.exp: This describes Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC), the most common skin malignancy. Mohs micrographic surgery offers the highest cure rate of >98% for primary BCC, making it the gold standard for high-risk or recurrent lesions.

questions.q: A 35-year-old HIV-positive patient presents with pruritic, hyperpigmented papules coalescing into plaques. Skin biopsy shows spindle cells, slit-like vascular spaces, extravasated RBCs, and hemosiderin deposits. What is the causative virus?
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma is caused by HHV-8 (Kaposi's Sarcoma-associated Herpesvirus, KSHV). It most commonly affects HIV-positive individuals and shows spindle cells and slit-like vascular spaces on histopathology.

questions.q: During a punch biopsy of the forearm, which layer of the skin contains the sensory nerve endings responsible for the sharp pain during incision?
questions.exp: The dermis contains the majority of sensory nerve endings (free nerve endings, Meissner's corpuscles in papillary dermis, Pacinian corpuscles in deeper dermis/subcutis). Pain during incision is primarily mediated by free nerve endings in the dermis.

questions.q: A 28-year-old atopic patient presents with chronic relapsing eczema. Filaggrin gene mutation is detected. Which of the following best explains the pathophysiology related to this mutation?
opts: Impaired skin barrier leading to increased transepidermal water loss and allergen sensitization
Increased IgE production by B lymphocytes
Decreased ceramide synthesis in stratum corneum
questions.exp: Filaggrin (FLG) mutations impair the skin barrier, causing increased transepidermal water loss (TEWL) and allowing penetration of allergens and microbes, triggering sensitization and the atopic march. This is the primary mechanism in atopic dermatitis.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with bilateral symmetrical brown patches on the forehead darkening in summer and fading in winter. She is on oral contraceptive pills. Wood's lamp examination shows enhancement of pigmentation. What layer is predominantly affected?
opts: Epidermal (increased melanin in basal and suprabasal layers)
questions.exp: Melasma on Wood's lamp (365 nm UV): epidermal type shows enhanced (accentuated) pigmentation, while dermal type does not enhance. This patient shows enhancement indicating predominantly epidermal melasma with increased melanin in basal and suprabasal layers.

questions.q: A 30-year-old male presents with erythematous scaly patches in the seborrhoeic areas (scalp, nasolabial folds, presternal area). KOH mount shows hyphae and spores. What is the first-line topical treatment?
questions.exp: Seborrhoeic dermatitis is associated with Malassezia furfur. First-line treatment is Ketoconazole 2% shampoo or cream targeting the yeast. Terbinafine has poor activity against Malassezia as it is a yeast, not a dermatophyte.

questions.q: A 16-year-old presents with condylomata acuminata (genital warts) typed as HPV 6 and 11. Which topical treatment works by stimulating local innate immunity as a Toll-like receptor 7 agonist?
questions.exp: Imiquimod is an immune response modifier that acts as a TLR-7 agonist, stimulating innate immunity and production of IFN-alpha and other cytokines. HPV 6 and 11 cause genital warts (low-risk types); HPV 16 and 18 are high-risk for carcinoma.

questions.q: A borderline lepromatous (BL) leprosy patient on MDT develops acute tender erythematous skin lesions, fever, and acute neuritis. The new lesions are distinct from original leprosy patches. What is this reaction and its treatment?
opts: Type 1 lepra reaction (reversal reaction) — treated with oral prednisolone
Type 2 lepra reaction (ENL) — treated with thalidomide
Type 1 reaction — treated with clofazimine alone
questions.exp: Type 1 (reversal) reaction occurs in borderline leprosy due to delayed hypersensitivity (Type IV). It manifests as upgrading of lesions with acute neuritis. Treatment is oral prednisolone 40–60 mg/day. MDT should be continued.

questions.q: A 19-year-old presents with multiple pearly, umbilicated papules on the trunk. Histopathology shows large intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies in keratinocytes. What are these inclusion bodies called?
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum (caused by a poxvirus, MCV) shows Henderson-Patterson bodies (molluscum bodies) — large eosinophilic intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies that compress the nucleus. Guarnieri bodies are seen in smallpox/vaccinia.

questions.q: A 65-year-old presents with a rapidly growing keratotic nodule on the cheek with a central keratin-filled crater reaching maximum size in 6–8 weeks then involuting spontaneously. Histopathology shows a cup-shaped lesion with well-differentiated squamous cells. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma (KA) is a rapidly growing, self-involuting benign tumour arising from hair follicle infundibulum. It shows a cup-shaped architecture with a central keratin plug on histopathology. Though considered benign, some classify it as a low-grade SCC variant.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman with dermatomyositis presents with violaceous erythema of the eyelids (heliotrope rash). Which auto-antibody is associated with increased risk of interstitial lung disease and antisynthetase syndrome?
questions.exp: Anti-Jo-1 antibody (anti-histidyl tRNA synthetase) is associated with antisynthetase syndrome: inflammatory myopathy + interstitial lung disease + mechanic's hands + Raynaud's. Anti-TIF1-gamma is associated with malignancy-associated dermatomyositis.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male with psoriasis on Methotrexate for 6 months needs a liver biopsy to assess fibrosis. According to Roenigk grading, which histological grade warrants discontinuation of Methotrexate?
questions.exp: Roenigk classification: Grade I (fatty infiltration, portal inflammation), Grade II (periportal fibrosis), Grade IIIA (septal fibrosis), Grade IIIB (bridging fibrosis), Grade IV (cirrhosis). MTX should be discontinued at Grade IIIB and IV.

questions.q: A 28-year-old female presents with annular erythematous plaques with fine scales trailing behind the advancing edge, distributed on trunk. Wood's lamp shows golden fluorescence. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Tinea corporis shows peripheral scaly ring with central clearing, caused by dermatophytes. Microsporum canis specifically shows golden-yellow fluorescence on Wood's lamp. Scales trail behind the advancing edge. Pityriasis rosea does not fluoresce.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with a painless penile ulcer. VDRL is reactive 1:32, TPHA is positive. He has no neurological symptoms. This is his first episode. What additional test is mandatory before starting treatment?
questions.exp: Before treating syphilis, HIV testing is mandatory because co-infection alters management (higher doses, longer treatment, need for CSF examination in neurosyphilis). Syphilis and HIV share transmission routes and are frequently co-diagnosed.

questions.q: A histopathology report describes 'acantholysis above the basal cell layer with a row of tombstone-like basal cells at the floor of the blister.' This finding is characteristic of which condition?
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris shows suprabasal acantholysis with a row of basal cells remaining attached to the dermis, giving the 'tombstone' or 'row of tombstones' appearance. Bullous pemphigoid shows subepidermal blistering without acantholysis.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with multiple hypopigmented macules on the trunk with fine branny scaling. KOH shows short hyphae and round spores ('spaghetti and meatballs'). What is the most effective single-dose oral treatment?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor (Malassezia furfur). Itraconazole 400 mg as a single oral dose (with exercise after 1–2 hours to promote sweating) is effective. Terbinafine has poor activity against Malassezia as it targets ergosterol synthesis differently.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male smoker presents with a verrucous, ulcerated lesion on the lower lip with indurated edges and regional lymphadenopathy. Biopsy shows well-differentiated SCC. What is the strongest risk factor for SCC of the lower lip?
opts: Chronic UV exposure and tobacco use
Marjolin's ulcer arising from a burn scar
questions.exp: SCC of the lip (especially lower lip) is strongly associated with chronic UV exposure and tobacco use. The lower lip receives more UV radiation due to its protrusion. HPV is more important for oropharyngeal and anogenital SCC.

questions.q: During patch testing for allergic contact dermatitis, the patient shows erythema, papules, and vesicles at Day 2 and Day 4 readings (scored ++). At what concentration is Nickel sulfate tested in the standard European baseline series?
questions.exp: Nickel sulfate is tested at 5% in petrolatum in the European standard baseline series. It is the most common contact allergen worldwide, frequently causing allergic contact dermatitis from jewelry, watches, and clothing fasteners.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman develops bluish-grey discolouration of sun-exposed areas after long-term use of a tetracycline for acne. The discolouration is due to drug-melanin complexes in the dermis. Which drug is responsible?
questions.exp: Minocycline causes three types of pigmentation: Type I (blue-black in acne scars), Type II (blue-grey on normal sun-exposed skin), and Type III (diffuse muddy-brown pigmentation). It forms complexes with melanin and iron in the dermis.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male presents with erythematous plaques with adherent scales on scalp, groin, and axillae. Dermoscopy shows a 'string of pearls' pattern of white scales around hair follicles. Skin biopsy shows PAS-positive spores within hair follicles. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Malassezia (Pityrosporum) folliculitis presents with perifollicular papules/pustules. Dermoscopy shows 'string of pearls' sign (white scales surrounding follicles). PAS-positive spores within follicles confirm the diagnosis. It is treated with oral itraconazole.
